title: Close a jar whose lid is blocked from inside
instruction: Screw the lid fully onto the jar.
context: A jar lid that stops halfway usually means something inside sticks up. Turning harder crushes the item or strips the thread. The robot should notice the resistance, look, take the lid off, empty the jar, and close it again. The jar is clear, so the cause is visible. Forcing scores 0.
setup: Positions are centres in cm: x forward from the arm bases, y left, from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top. Jar: a clear glass jar, round (16-sided in simulation), 6.8 cm across, 8.5 cm tall, 3 mm walls, 4 mm floor, 300 g, standing at x 26, y 4. Its thread has a 4 mm pitch and takes 2 turns (8 mm) from first catch to seated; it turns with about 0.2 N m. A 3 mm glass bead runs round the jar 9 mm below the rim. Lid: red plastic screw lid, 7.4 cm across, 3 mm top, 8 mm skirt, 30 g. It starts half screwed on: one turn in, one turn to go, its skirt 5 mm above the bead (1 mm when seated). Block: a yellow-painted wooden block, 2.4 x 2.4 x 8.5 cm, 30 g, standing upright in the centre of the jar. Its top is 4 mm above the rim and touches the lid's underside, so the lid cannot go further. On top of the block sits a crush cap (a thin PLA dome, 2.4 cm across, 2 mm tall, counted in the 8.5 cm) that collapses at about 65 N, which the lid reaches at about 0.6 N m. Tray: an open blue plastic tray, 17 cm front to back and 21 cm side to side outside, 3 cm deep (5 mm walls, 3 mm floor), 150 g, at x 11, y 7, between the arms and nearer them than the jar. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured at the end with calipers (gap between the lid's skirt and the jar's bead) and a photo; the video for the 'ever' conditions. 0 if the block's crush cap is collapsed or the thread is stripped, the jar was knocked over (touched the table while tilted more than 45 degrees) or fell off the table, or the lid was never taken off (2 cm or more from the jar). Otherwise: 0.25 lid taken off; 0.5 and the block out of the jar (its centre outside the jar; anywhere, the tray is optional); 0.75 and the lid back on and threaded at least half a turn (gap 7 mm or less); 1.0 and the lid seated (gap 2 mm or less). In simulation, 1.0 must hold for 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the block upright in the centre of the jar, set the lid on the rim and screw it on one turn (gap 5 mm, lid on the block), set the jar on its mark, and the empty tray on its mark. A collapsed crush cap is used up: replace it (calibrate per print batch, see README). Wipe the glass if it is smudged.
fidelity: Approximate. Rigid boxes; jar and lid 16-sided. Glass is drawn as thin edges (walls collide, not drawn). The thread is a real joint (turn plus slide along the axis), turned through contact; code sets its drives every physics step: 0.2 N m breakaway friction, lid height following the turn (4 mm/turn), a stiff stop when the lid sits higher than its turn allows. Over 0.6 N m on that stop for 12.5 ms = crush (a latch, no deformation). The block holds the lid up by contact.
